stem: Which of the following forms accounts for most carbon dioxide transport in human blood?

options.label: A
options.text: Dissolved CO2 gas in plasma alone
options.misconception: The small dissolved fraction is being treated as the majority.
options.explanation: Only a small fraction of CO2 travels as dissolved gas; about 70% is carried as bicarbonate.

options.label: B
options.misconception: None; roughly 70% of CO2 is transported as bicarbonate.
options.explanation: Most carbon dioxide is converted in red cells to bicarbonate, which then travels in plasma as the main transport form.

options.label: C
options.text: Carbamino compounds on plasma albumin only
options.misconception: A minority carbamino route is being overstated.
options.explanation: Some CO2 binds proteins as carbamino compounds, but bicarbonate is the predominant transport form.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Platelets are being invented as a CO2 carrier.
options.explanation: CO2 transport is a red-cell/plasma process (dissolved, carbamino, bicarbonate), not a platelet function.

options.label: E
options.text: Unmodified CO2 trapped in alveolar surfactant
options.misconception: Lung lining fluid is being confused with blood transport.
options.explanation: Surfactant reduces alveolar surface tension; it does not carry systemic CO2 in blood.

context: Learning objective: name the dominant CO2 transport form. About 70% of CO2 travels as bicarbonate after red-cell carbonic anhydrase conversion.
